info.name: Socialstats API
info.description:
API Access to Creator and Social Content Data

Enterprise API collection generated from docs/socialstats_openapi.yaml and live Rails Enterprise routes.
Set the `api_key` collection variable before sending authenticated requests. The collection uses the `apikey` header for authentication. Creator link mutations require the matching `add_link_request` or `remove_link_request` permission plus creator object access. OAuth callback/status endpoints may also support short-lived state-token access as documented.

Creator-dependent endpoints accept `socialstats_creator_id` or one of `instagram_creator_id`, `facebook_creator_id`, `youtube_creator_id`, and `tiktok_creator_id`. Each source-specific selector accepts either the platform internal ID (`external_id`) or exact username (`secondary_id`). Use one creator selector per request.

Creator info `links` objects include both `external_id` and `username`; `username` is null when the source has no stored username or handle.

The Authorization folder contains the complete creator backstage OAuth workflow, provider scopes, polling steps, and status guidance.

Successful responses use `result` and `message` plus the documented resource key. Error responses consistently use `result: error` and `message`. Public and authorized post current-stat responses use the same nested `stats.<group>.<timeframe>` structure.

Postman exports collections as JSON. This file uses the Postman Collection v2.1 schema.

Metric consistency: Public post totals retain the same meaning with and without authorization. Complete provider-specific values are under stats.authorized.data in authorized current responses and under authorized in each authorized history row. Missing values are omitted or null, not zero. Ordinary post counters use the latest equivalent measurement. TikTok profile counters prefer successful authorized measurements for four days, then accept newer public measurements. Provider corrections and changes in the measurement provider are not reliable organic growth. Revoked access immediately hides restricted metrics.

Regular analytics endpoints use existing channel authorization automatically. Member and entity keys reuse their owning member's active dashboard channel connections. Entity keys also accept grants belonging to their agreement; other Enterprise key types use only agreement grants. Set data_access=public to request public data only. Check data_access_used, is_authorized, and authorization_status in each source or post response. Facebook posts and Instagram stories require owner channel authorization; lists omit them and post-detail requests return 403 without it or in public mode. Public posts from other profiles remain available.

Member key lifecycle: Member API keys have one current credential per member. Disabling or regenerating a member key also prevents legacy duplicate credentials from authorizing requests. Creating an MCP connection preserves an existing agreement's disabled state and administrator permissions. Temporarily disabled member keys can be enabled by explicit regeneration in Account settings; permanently disabled keys require support review. These rules do not combine separate Enterprise agreements or their accounting histories.

Consent is checked for the exact provider and owning channel. Public Instagram responses omit photo/carousel views, shares, saves, reposts and Story metrics across current stats, histories and content lists. Rankings exclude posts whose requested metric is unavailable before pagination. A connection to one channel or collaborator does not authorize another owner. Explicit public mode excludes private insights even with an active grant. Public TikTok shares and observed zero counters remain available; missing counters are omitted.

Facebook follower countries and cities are connected-account Page Insights, returned only for the exact authorized channels and omitted from public mode and the public country drilldown.

request.description:
Returns creator metadata and public source links. A link includes connection status only when its source is assigned to the API key and supports channel authorization.
Generated from docs/socialstats_openapi.yaml.

Query parameters:
- socialstats_creator_id (optional): The public 8-character Socialstats ID. Supply this or exactly one source-specific creator selector.
- instagram_creator_id (optional): Instagram internal ID or exact username. Use only one creator selector per request.
- facebook_creator_id (optional): Facebook internal ID or exact username. Use only one creator selector per request.
- youtube_creator_id (optional): YouTube channel ID or exact channel handle. Use only one creator selector per request.
- tiktok_creator_id (optional): TikTok internal ID or exact username. Use only one creator selector per request.
- with_links (optional): Includes all public source links associated with the requested creator. Connection status is shown only for sources assigned to the API Key. Example: true.

request.description:
Returns creator history over the requested date range. Public and connected-account histories are merged by date where this key is authorized; otherwise only public history is returned. TikTok keeps observed public creator totals across linked profiles, including zero; connected history fills gaps without replacing those totals. Connection expiry can reduce the available fields. Use data_access=public to exclude connected-account data. Each source reports data_access_used and its connection status. See the Public Data and Authorized Data response examples where provided.

Public YouTube, Instagram and Facebook post views, likes and comments select one complete history per post and metric. With automatic data access and permitted owner authorization, authorized history is preferred when that metric was observed within the seven UTC dates ending today; otherwise public history is used if available, retaining permitted older authorized history only when public history is absent. Public mode excludes authorized history. Missing counters are omitted, measured zero is valid, and no undated current total or mixed-source prefix/suffix is appended. Authorized daily counts accumulate only retained reporting periods, so a graph endpoint can differ from current stats. Shares and other private insights, including Instagram Story/photo insight views, retain their existing behavior.

Consent is checked for the exact provider and owning channel. Public Instagram responses omit photo/carousel views, shares, saves, reposts and Story metrics across current stats, histories and content lists. Rankings exclude posts whose requested metric is unavailable before pagination. A connection to one channel or collaborator does not authorize another owner. Explicit public mode excludes private insights even with an active grant. Public TikTok shares and observed zero counters remain available; missing counters are omitted.

Send each date parameter at most once. An invalid date range is rejected before an entity slot is reserved.

If supplied, legacy limit and offset values must each be a single query value. Malformed shapes are rejected before quota accounting.

request.description:
Returns the latest activities for a creator filtered by source.
Generated from docs/socialstats_openapi.yaml.

Query parameters:
- source (required): Specifies the Socialstats sources being requested. Can be a comma separated list of individual sources or be set to 'all'. Surrounding whitespace on source names is allowed. Analytics are limited to sources assigned to the API key. Send source only once as a string, not an array or object. Creator-level endpoints support youtube, instagram, facebook, and tiktok. Public post-level content supports instagram, youtube, and tiktok. Authorized post-level content also supports facebook. Example: instagram,youtube,tiktok.
- socialstats_creator_id (optional): The public 8-character Socialstats ID. Supply this or exactly one source-specific creator selector.
- instagram_creator_id (optional): Instagram internal ID or exact username. Use only one creator selector per request.
- facebook_creator_id (optional): Facebook internal ID or exact username. Use only one creator selector per request.
- youtube_creator_id (optional): YouTube channel ID or exact channel handle. Use only one creator selector per request.
- tiktok_creator_id (optional): TikTok internal ID or exact username. Use only one creator selector per request.
- limit (optional): Specifies the limit of results being returned. The maximum limit is 100. Example: 20.
- offset (optional): Specifies the offset of the limited results being returned. Activity endpoints accept at most one integer for each of limit, offset, and tier. The limit must be from 1 to 100; offsets must be from 0 to 2147483647. Example: 20.
- milestones (optional): Include Milestone Activities. Example: true.
- comments (optional): Include Comment Activities. Example: true.
- tier (optional): Filter Activities by importance. Tier 4 is the lowest tier that returns all activities. Tier 1 is the highest tier that returns only the most significant activities. Example: 4.

Headers:
- Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate, br

Documented responses: 200, 400, 401, 403, 404, 429, 500, 502, 503.

Public post totals retain the same meaning with and without authorization. Complete provider-specific values are under stats.authorized.data in authorized current responses and under authorized in each authorized history row. Missing values are omitted or null, not zero. Ordinary post counters use the latest equivalent measurement. TikTok profile counters prefer successful authorized measurements for four days, then accept newer public measurements. Provider corrections and changes in the measurement provider are not reliable organic growth. Revoked access immediately hides restricted metrics.

Activity provenance: public milestone and Standout alerts use public counters and comparison posts. Private variants require current exact owning-channel authorization. data_access=public excludes private alerts and selects a proven public variant when available, including its rank before pagination. Legacy Standout alerts without proven public provenance require owner authorization, except public-only TikTok alerts. Instagram Story view milestones are excluded; authorized Standout Stories remain available. Comment alerts inherit their parent post access: Facebook posts and Instagram Stories require current exact owner-channel authorization, including alerts created before access changed.

URL that Socialstats redirects to after the platform callback. HTTPS is required except for localhost. Non-reserved query pairs and the fragment are preserved, including repeated/bracketed keys and empty flags. Callback result keys replace existing values once; absent optional callback fields remove older values for the same exact key.
Optional customer-side string returned unchanged throughout creation, status responses and callbacks, including whitespace, punctuation and Unicode. Non-string values are rejected.
Optional customer platform string stored with the authorization.

request.description:
Creates a short-lived platform OAuth URL that a creator can open to authorize backstage Socialstats access. The returned state token is carried through the callback and can be used for browser-side status polling without exposing the API Key. The creator must grant every configured provider scope; partial consent fails with `missing_scope`. Send exactly one creator selector and one source selector. Do not repeat selectors across the query and body.
Generated from docs/socialstats_openapi.yaml.

Query parameters:
- socialstats_creator_id (optional): The public 8-character Socialstats ID. Supply this or exactly one source-specific creator selector.
- instagram_creator_id (optional): Instagram internal ID or exact username. Use only one creator selector per request.
- facebook_creator_id (optional): Facebook internal ID or exact username. Use only one creator selector per request.
- youtube_creator_id (optional): YouTube channel ID or exact channel handle. Use only one creator selector per request.
- tiktok_creator_id (optional): TikTok internal ID or exact username. Use only one creator selector per request.
- source_id (required): The social source being authorized. Example: youtube.
- return_url (optional): HTTPS URL that Socialstats should redirect the browser to after the platform callback. Localhost HTTP URLs are accepted for development. Example: https://customer.example.com/socialstats/oauth-return.
- external_reference (optional): Customer-side identifier carried through the authorization flow and returned in status responses. Example: client_creator_123.
- platform (optional): Customer platform metadata stored with the authorization. The provider flow remains server-side web OAuth. Example: web.

Headers:
- Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate, br

Documented responses: 200, 400, 401, 403, 404. Current agreement, creator/product, source and analytics permissions are rechecked before exchange and activation. Lost access returns `failed`; a source moved to another creator returns `wrong_profile`. Token, grant, member-confirmation and initial-sync request writes commit together. Connected Meta grants are limited to permitted sources and never reassign another creator profile. The existing job-request dispatcher hands off committed initial-sync requests; TikTok metadata refreshes in that sync. An attempt created before grant revocation cannot reactivate that grant, including a connected Meta source; create a new authorization URL to reauthorize after revocation. A later successful reauthorization does not make an older pending URL usable again. Canonical Creator merges retain grants and pending attempts under the surviving Creator, preserving provider identity and revocation history; current API Key and member subscription permissions remain required.

Customer external_reference strings are preserved unchanged, including whitespace, punctuation and Unicode; non-string values are rejected. Send `return_url`, `external_reference` and `platform` at most once each as strings, in either the query or body. Existing non-reserved return_url query pairs retain their order and encoding, including repeated/bracketed keys and empty flags. The fragment is preserved. Invalid return URLs are rejected at creation. The exact callback fields result, status, message, source_id, socialstats_creator_id and external_reference replace older values once; absent optional callback fields remove older values for their exact key.

item.description:
# Creator Backstage Authorization

Authorize one creator and one source at a time for YouTube, Instagram, Facebook, or TikTok.

## Flow

1. Set `api_key`, one creator selector, and `authorization_source_id`.
2. Send **Create OAuth Authorization URL**.
3. Copy the returned `state_token` into the collection variable and open `authorization_url` in the creator's browser. The attempt expires after 30 minutes.
4. The creator selects the exact linked profile and grants every requested scope. Socialstats handles the callback and validates the profile identity.
5. Poll **Get OAuth Attempt Status** until `status` changes from `pending`. This request does not use the API Key. If the create request included `return_url`, Socialstats also redirects there with the final result.
6. Send **List OAuth Authorizations** with the API Key. Access is usable when `status` is `active` and `is_authorized` is `true`. Member and entity keys also reuse their owning member's dashboard confirmations; those inherited entries have no grant id and must be disconnected in the dashboard. Revoking an entity key's agreement grant leaves an independent dashboard confirmation in place.
7. Use the authorized creator and post requests. Revoke only this API Key's grant with **Revoke OAuth Authorization** when access should end.

Do not manually send **Platform OAuth Callback**; providers call it directly.

## Required Scopes

- **YouTube:** `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/youtube.readonly`, `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/yt-analytics.readonly`
- **Meta / Facebook / Instagram:** `email`, `instagram_basic`, `instagram_manage_comments`, `pages_manage_metadata`, `pages_read_user_content`, `instagram_manage_insights`, `pages_read_engagement`, `read_insights`, `pages_show_list`, `business_management`
- **TikTok:** `user.info.basic`, `user.info.stats`, `user.info.profile`, `video.list`

Every configured scope is mandatory. Common terminal statuses include `active`, `expired_attempt`, `missing_scope`, `wrong_profile`, `wrong_source`, `missing_profile`, `provider_error`, `token_expired`, and `revoked`. Instagram and Facebook have additional Page/profile matching statuses documented in the API guide.
